entities.summary:
Guttation is a phenomenon of water loss through small pores, or hydathodes, found at the end of veins in leaves. 

This process is a vital mechanism for plants to release excess xylem sap, which helps maintain their water balance and prevents damage to the plant. 

Guttation plays a crucial role in the survival and adaptation of plants in various environments, from arid to humid conditions. 


A fascinating example of plant resilience, guttation has no direct impact on human history, but it is an intriguing aspect of plant biology.
